title: unified rollouts: probing/quarantine + metric-quorum autorollback
author: Evan Liu
release_notes: Adds probing/quarantine stage to staged shadow rollouts and implements metric-quorum autorollback policy. Includes e2e tests and telemetry.
description: Motivation: Improve rollout safety for staged shadow and canary workflows by adding a probing/quarantine stage that can hold suspicious traffic while additional metrics are gathered, and by implementing a metric-quorum based autorollback to avoid noisy single-metric triggers. This PR implements the probing/quarantine stage in the unified rollout controller, plumbs new lifecycle states through the policy engine, and adds a configurable metric-quorum threshold for autorollback decisions. Main changes: 1) rollout controller: add Probe and Quarantine states, new transition conditions, and explicit TTL for quarantine; 2) autorollback engine: support composite metric quorums (n of m metrics must exceed thresholds) and per-stage sensitivity; 3) observability: new rollout.telemetry.{probe_enter,probe_exit,quarantine_enter,quarantine_exit,autorollback_decision} metrics and structured logs for decisions; 4) e2e/tests: stability tests for staged shadow probing and deliberate flapping scenarios; 5) docs: rollout policy reference and migration notes. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4772) - [x] Implementation of Probe/Quarantine states - [x] Metric-quorum autorollback engine - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] E2E stability tests in perf-canary harness - [x] Updated docs and release notes - [x] Security review for rollout metadata exposure Migration notes: existing rollout configs are backward compatible. New behavior is opt-in via rollout.policy.stage_config.probing.enabled and rollout.policy.autorollback.metric_quorum. Default deployment behavior remains unchanged. Testing notes: Added e2e scenarios that simulate transient metric spikes, slow regressions, and noisy signals to validate quarantine TTL and quota behavior. CI included an integration test using the perf-canary harness and a canary against a small model pool to validate routing and KV cache behavior under staged shadow traffic. Related: references ENG-4820 (telemetry spec) and SUP-903 (customer incident that motivated quarantine stage).
commits: feat(rollouts): add Probe and Quarantine lifecycle states; feat(autorollback): metric-quorum evaluation and decision pipeline; perf(rollouts): limit probe sampling to 10% by default; test(e2e): add staged-shadow probing tests; docs: rollout policy doc and migration notes; ci: add perf-canary scenario and retries for flaky tests

rollouts/autorollback.py - metric-quorum evaluator and decision handler (approx 180 lines)
rollouts/policy_schema.yaml - new probing and metric_quorum fields
telemetry/metrics.py - new rollout.* metrics and tags
docs/rollouts.md - policy docs and migration section
review_thread: Maya: Can you clarify quarantine TTL rationale? Suggested making TTL configurable per-tenant. Evan: TTL made configurable via rollout.policy.stage_config.probing.quarantine_ttl and default set to 30s to match current probe cadence. Luis: Concern about false positives if metric instrumentation lags; requested adding a 1-min warmup window and explicit metric staleness checks. Evan: Added staleness guard and warmup window; updated tests to simulate delayed metrics. Priya: Please add e2e that shows recovery path from quarantine to stable when telemetry returns. Evan: Added e2e scenario and updated structured logs to include decision traces. Review approvals: Luis and Priya approved after follow-ups; Maya approved after TTL change. Final: non-blocking comment from Security about exposing rollout IDs in logs, addressed with redaction and minimal IDs.
ci: CI run summary: initial push triggered unit tests + integration + e2e. Unit tests: pass. Integration (rollouts) failed on flakey test 'test_quarantine_ttl_flap' due to timing assumptions. Fix: adjusted test timing and added retry-based assertion. Rerun: all tests passed. Perf-canary scenario executed (best-effort, short run) and reported no regressions in average 95th pct latency for small model pool. Lint: pass. OSS-compat checks: pass. Final CI status: pass.
